title: A Inventory for the Language
premise: Quentin Sandoval, a piano tuner who reads houses through their radiators and pipes, has spent seven years in the orbit of the Vane family, tuning their instruments and never quite confessing that he was the last person to see their son alive. When a box of undelivered letters surfaces behind a wardrobe during a house clearance, Quentin is pulled into delivering them at last — each one addressed to someone who believed Theo Vane died by accident. Returning to the coastal town where the story went wrong, Quentin must choose between protecting the family's fragile loyalty to a comforting lie and telling the truth he has carried like an untuned string. The book ends with Quentin playing the restored piano for the assembled family, saying it plainly at last, and discovering that truth, delivered late, can still be received.
about_author: S. M. Dunmore is the pen name of a former piano restorer who spent a decade working in old houses along the Atlantic coast before turning to fiction. Their writing is known for its attention to sound, domestic architecture, and the small betrayals families commit out of love.

chapters.title: The Pitch of Old Houses
chapters.summary: Quentin, POV, tunes a neglected upright in the Vane house and describes how he hears history in radiators and pipes. He notes the wardrobe being moved for a house clearance. Emotional beat: quiet dread beneath professional calm, establishing his seven years of almost-saying-it.

chapters.title: Behind the Wardrobe
chapters.summary: The movers find a tin box wedged behind plaster; Quentin recognizes the handwriting instantly as Theo's. Marianne Vane asks him to hold it until she decides. POV: Quentin. Beat: the past physically dislodged from the walls of the present.

chapters.title: Seven Years of Almost
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter in Quentin's POV: the night Theo died, what Quentin saw from the boathouse, and why he let the accident narrative stand. Beat: guilt rendered as a permanently flat note he cannot correct.

chapters.title: An Inventory of Undelivered Things
chapters.summary: Quentin catalogs the letters at his kitchen table — eleven envelopes, none stamped, each addressed with unsettling precision. One is addressed to him. POV: Quentin. Beat: compulsion; he cannot put the box down any more than he could put down the truth.

chapters.title: Marianne Decides
chapters.summary: Marianne summons Quentin and her surviving children, Iris and Callum, and announces they will deliver the letters in person, together, before the house is sold. POV shifts to Iris. Beat: reluctant unity forged around a box no one wants opened.

chapters.title: Letter One: To the Lighthouse Keeper
chapters.summary: The first letter goes to elderly Nels Farrow, who reads it aloud and reveals Theo visited him weeks before his death asking about the tide charts. POV: Callum. Beat: first crack in the official story; Callum's loyalty to his dead brother wavers into curiosity.

chapters.title: The Road Back to Salt Hollow
chapters.summary: The family drives to the coastal town where Theo grew up and died; Quentin navigates by memory he pretends not to have. POV: Quentin. Beat: dread of geography — every landmark accuses him.

chapters.title: Letter Two: To the Girl Who Left
chapters.summary: They find Dana Okafor, Theo's first love, now a marine biologist. Her letter contains a pressed flower and an apology without explanation. POV: Dana via Iris's observation. Beat: tenderness and irritation — Theo loved people enough to apologize but not enough to explain.

chapters.title: What the Boathouse Remembers
chapters.summary: Quentin visits the boathouse alone at night, unable to sleep. He stands where he stood seven years ago. POV: Quentin. Beat: the reader learns more than the family knows — Quentin heard Theo arguing with someone.

chapters.title: Iris Suspects
chapters.summary: Iris notices Quentin flinched at the boathouse and begins quietly assembling his evasions into a pattern. POV: Iris. Beat: suspicion as grief's sharp twin; she needs someone to blame and Quentin is conveniently near.

chapters.title: Letter Three: To My Father
chapters.summary: The letter to patriarch Edmund Vane is unopened because Edmund refuses it, insisting Theo's affairs are settled. POV: Callum. Beat: the generational wall — loyalty to a version of Theo that requires no questions.

chapters.title: The Tuner's Confession, Partially
chapters.summary: Under Iris's pressure, Quentin admits he was at the boathouse that night but claims he arrived after. A half-truth that satisfies no one. POV: Quentin. Beat: the art of almost-saying-it failing for the first time.

chapters.title: Letter Four: To the Doctor
chapters.summary: Dr. Prasad receives a letter revealing Theo had been diagnosed with a degenerative condition and told no one. POV: Iris. Beat: reframing — Theo's secrecy had medical roots, complicating everyone's anger.

chapters.title: Nels Farrow's Second Story
chapters.summary: Nels calls Iris: he remembered more. Theo asked specifically about the night tides on a particular date — the date of his death. POV: Iris. Beat: the accident theory begins to drown.

chapters.title: Callum's Ledger
chapters.summary: Callum, an accountant, starts a private ledger reconciling dates, letters, and lies, treating the mystery like arithmetic. POV: Callum. Beat: loyalty vs. truth embodied — his columns keep refusing to balance in Edmund's favor.

chapters.title: Letter Five: To the Boy on the Pier
chapters.summary: A letter addressed to a teenager, Jonah, whom nobody in the family has ever heard of. They track him to a nearby town. POV: Quentin. Beat: the widening circle — Theo had an entire hidden life of debts and kindnesses.

chapters.title: Jonah Tells It Sideways
chapters.summary: Jonah, now twenty, reveals Theo paid for his mother's surgery anonymously and once said, 'Tell them I was happy.' POV: Jonah via Callum. Beat: warmth braided with foreboding — happiness stated that deliberately sounds like farewell.

chapters.title: Edmund Breaks a Glass
chapters.summary: Edmund confronts the group, accusing them of exhuming a boy who deserves rest. Marianne, for the first time, contradicts him. POV: Iris. Beat: the marriage's fault line exposed; loyalty itself splits by generation.

chapters.title: Letter Six: To Q.S.
chapters.summary: The letter addressed to Quentin. He reads it alone: Theo knew Quentin saw something, and wrote, 'You were kind to stay silent. Don't be.' POV: Quentin. Beat: devastating permission — the dead man absolving and indicting him in one line.

chapters.title: What Quentin Heard
chapters.summary: Full flashback: Quentin heard Theo argue with Edmund about money Theo had been moving out of family accounts — and then watched Theo walk toward the water alone, deliberately. POV: Quentin. Beat: the secret fully revealed to the reader; suicide disguised as accident.

chapters.title: The House Clearance
chapters.summary: Back home, the Vane house is emptied room by room; Quentin tunes the piano one last time before it ships. POV: Iris. Beat: elegy — a family's material memory packed into crates while its emotional debts remain unpacked.

chapters.title: Letter Seven: To the Bank Manager
chapters.summary: A dry, procedural letter that nonetheless confirms Theo liquidated everything over six months, methodically settling every account. POV: Callum. Beat: horror of intentionality — this was planned like an inventory.

chapters.title: Marianne's Own Letter
chapters.summary: Marianne admits she found one of Theo's letters years ago and burned it, choosing comfort over truth. POV: Marianne. Beat: the theme crystallized — she committed Quentin's sin first, and bigger.

chapters.title: Iris Confronts Quentin
chapters.summary: Iris, having pieced it together, demands the whole truth on the pier where Theo died. Quentin gives her everything except the final sentence. POV: alternating close-third. Beat: two people holding opposite halves of the same grief.

chapters.title: Letter Eight: To My Brother
chapters.summary: Callum finally opens his own letter: Theo apologizes for leaving him the family, knowing Callum would carry Edmund's denial alone. POV: Callum. Beat: grief as inheritance — the true legacy Theo left was this burden.

chapters.title: Edmund's Heart
chapters.summary: Edmund suffers a cardiac episode amid the revelations; in the hospital he grips Quentin's wrist and says only, 'He asked me to go with him.' POV: Quentin. Beat: the father knew — and chose silence too, making Quentin's silence part of a family tradition.

chapters.title: The Ninth Letter Is Missing
chapters.summary: Counting the envelopes, they discover one referenced in Theo's journal never made it into the box. Someone destroyed it. POV: Iris. Beat: paranoia and urgency — time running out as the house sale closes and witnesses scatter.

chapters.title: Nels Farrow Dies
chapters.summary: Nels passes peacefully, leaving Iris a note: 'Tides don't lie, girl. Check the ninth.' POV: Iris. Beat: mortality compressing the timeline; the living archive shrinking.

chapters.title: The Search for the Ninth
chapters.summary: Quentin tears apart the cleared house, listening to its pipes the way he listens to pianos, and finds the ninth letter taped inside the piano's soundboard — where Theo knew only the tuner would look. POV: Quentin. Beat: revelation through craft; Theo trusted Quentin's ears all along.

chapters.title: Letter Nine: To Whoever Finds This
chapters.summary: Theo's true final letter: a clear-eyed account of his decision, releasing everyone from blame except the silence itself. 'Say it out loud or it will say you.' POV: Quentin reading aloud. Beat: the dead man's voice finally tuned to pitch.

chapters.title: Edmund's Choice
chapters.summary: From his hospital bed, Edmund must decide whether to confirm the truth publicly or maintain the lie with his remaining strength. POV: Callum. Beat: loyalty vs. truth reaching its terminal fork in the family's oldest member.

chapters.title: The Gathering
chapters.summary: Marianne convenes everyone — family, Dana, Jonah, Dr. Prasad — in the emptied house for one evening before closing. POV: Iris. Beat: held breath; the house itself seems to wait.

chapters.title: Quentin Says It
chapters.summary: Quentin tells the whole truth aloud: what he heard, what he saw, what he withheld and why. No art of almost. POV: Quentin. Beat: climax — seven years of flat note resolved into a clean, terrible chord.

chapters.title: Edmund Speaks
chapters.summary: Edmund, wheeled in against doctors' advice, confirms it and asks his family's forgiveness for teaching them that love means lying well. POV: Callum. Beat: the second blow of the climax; the patriarch's confession shatters and rebuilds the family in one motion.

chapters.title: What the Family Does With Truth
chapters.summary: Aftermath scenes: anger, weeping, Dana and Jonah trading stories of Theo, Iris laughing for the first time in chapters. POV: rotating. Beat: catharsis — truth delivered late still lands, and lands softer than feared.

chapters.title: The Piano Arrives
chapters.summary: The restored piano is delivered to Marianne's new cottage; Quentin tunes it while the family watches, understanding now what his listening meant. POV: Quentin. Beat: reconciliation through vocation — his gift for hearing what houses hide becomes a gift for letting families hear themselves.

chapters.title: Letters Forwarded
chapters.summary: Epistolary interlude: copies of all nine letters, annotated by each recipient with what they did after receiving them. POV: documentary collage. Beat: the inventory completed — every undelivered thing finally at its address.

chapters.title: Iris Keeps the House Key
chapters.summary: Iris visits the sold, empty Vane house with a copy of the key, says goodbye to the radiator's hum, and leaves the key under the door for whoever comes next. POV: Iris. Beat: release — inheritance redefined as what you carry, not what you own.

chapters.title: A Tuning at Sea Level
chapters.summary: Quentin takes a new commission in Salt Hollow, tuning a church piano, and visits Theo's grave to report, conversationally, that everyone knows now and no one has left. POV: Quentin. Beat: peace earned rather than granted; guilt transmuted into ongoing care.

chapters.title: Coda: The Sound of a House Telling the Truth
chapters.summary: Final chapter: months later, the scattered family gathers at Marianne's for music. Quentin plays; the letters sit in an open box on the mantel, delivered, read, kept. POV: Quentin. Beat: resolution — found family, honest inheritance, and the loyalty that survives truth instead of replacing it.
